# Windows sandboxes: mount the workspace at `/workspaces/<rel>` and translate paths at the manager's edge

## What to build

graph-manager (`apps/graph-manager`) starts a sandboxed run in a Linux container and mounts the workspace **at its own host path**, because the engine stores absolute paths. On a Windows host that path (`C:\Users\me\graph-manager-workspaces\github\octo\hello`) cannot be a mount target. This slice makes `win32` work without changing the engine:

- a new pure module `src/server/sandbox-paths.ts` (`containerRoot`, `toContainer`, `toHost`, `toContainerArgs`);
- on `win32`, `Sandboxes.start` mounts the workspace at `/workspaces/<rel>`, hands the container its working directory, ready file, reviewers file and path arguments in that form, runs it as `1000:1000`, and passes git settings as `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables; graph-manager keeps using host paths for its own file access;
- reading a sandboxed run's `state.json` (`runs.ts` `runDetail`, used by the UI and by Create PR) puts `tasksDir` and `specPath` back in host form;
- the fake Docker daemon writes the ready file through the bind mounts, so the start-to-ready path runs with `platform: "win32"` on any OS.

Everything is selected by one value, `Sandboxes.platform`. On Linux and macOS every output stays byte-for-byte what it is today. The work happens on Linux; CI runs the tests on ubuntu, macos and windows (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`).

What the previous task delivered (it is in the code): `new Sandboxes({ config, store, docker?, platform? })` with `readonly platform: NodeJS.Platform` (default `process.platform`); `new DockerClient(socketPath, platform)`; `inspectSelf()` answers `undefined` on `win32` and `darwin`, so `this.self` is never set there; `startFakeDocker({ osType })`; `defaultDockerSocket` in `config.ts`.

Scope limits: edit only, under `apps/graph-manager`, `src/server/sandbox-paths.ts` (new) and its test, `sandbox-run.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `runs.ts`, the comment in `routes/internal.ts`, `scripts/fake-docker.mjs`, and the tests named below. `routes/runs.ts`, `routes/resume.ts`, `pr.ts`, `docker.ts`, `config.ts` and `sandbox-tools.ts` need **no** change. Do not edit the engine (`packages/graph-execution`), any README, `TESTING.md` or `docs/`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/workspaces.ts` (lines 6–17, 21–30) — `Workspace`: `id` (`github~octo~hello`), `path` (absolute, host separators), `rel` (`github/octo/hello`, always `/`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts` — `sandboxEnv` (lines 153–189; line 183 builds the ready file from `p.runDir`), `gitIdentity` (192–209), `workspaceMount` (211–232), `containerBody` (234–281; `User`, `Cmd`, `WorkingDir`), `PASSED` (131–143: `GIT_CONFIG_*` is not passed from graph-manager's own env).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` — `StartParams` (94–106), `start` (490–668): `runDir`/`readyFile` (558–560), owner from `stat` (561–562), the reviewers copy (573–585), `sandboxEnv` and the reviewers variable (587–596), mounts (597), `containerBody` (598–611), the wait for the ready file (639–667); `prepareTools` (781–808).
- Callers of `start` (read, do not change): `routes/runs.ts` line 117 (`cwd: ws.path`, args from `startArgs`: `[tasksDir, "--spec", spec, "--provider", p, …]`, both relative to the workspace as the browser sent them), `routes/resume.ts` lines 52–60 (`args: ["--resume", "--run", runId]`), `routes/internal.ts` lines 114–159 (a terminal's `graph-execution … --sandbox`: `cwd` is the terminal's folder inside the workspace, `args` are what the user typed, relative to `cwd` or absolute). `scanArgs` (`routes/internal.ts` lines 34–55) shows how positionals and value options are told apart.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runs.ts` — `SandboxLookup` and `setSandboxLookup` (121–136), `readState` (163–170), `summarize` (229–260), `readTasks` (325), `runDetail` (485–513; line 496 reads the state, line 499 reads `state.tasksDir`). `pr.ts` lines 108–118 and 199 take `specPath` from `runDetail`.
- `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs` — `bindRewrite` (256–263), `startPassive` (326–345).
- Tests: `sandbox-run.test.ts`, `sandbox.test.ts` (the `NoTools` subclass, lines 38–53), `runs.test.ts` (lines 24–62 fixtures, 164–185 the lookup test, 218–245 `runDetail`), `routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts` (lines 67–108), `routes/internal.test.ts` (lines 108–130), `sandbox-tools.test.ts` (lines 40–63), `vitest.config.ts`.
- Engine, read only: `packages/graph-execution/src/runner/run.ts` lines 176–197 (what goes into `state.json`), `src/state/state.ts` line 89 (`sandbox`).

## Patterns to follow

**How a run is known to be sandboxed.** The engine writes `sandbox: { image }` into `state.json` whenever `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX=1` (`run.ts` line 193), and graph-manager always sets that variable (`sandbox-run.ts` line 176). The marker stays after the container and its record in `graph-manager.json` are gone, so `state.sandbox !== undefined` is the test; no store lookup is needed.

**Reading git config** (`sandbox-run.ts` lines 192–197):

```typescript
const get = async (key: string): Promise<string | undefined> => {
  const res = await execa("git", ["config", "--get", key], { cwd, reject: false });
  const v = typeof res.stdout === "string" ? res.stdout.trim() : "";
  return res.exitCode === 0 && v !== "" ? v : undefined;
};
```

**The fake daemon maps container paths through bind mounts** (`fake-docker.mjs` line 256); today only exec mode uses it:

```javascript
function bindRewrite(c, value) {
  let out = value;
  for (const m of c.HostConfig?.Mounts ?? []) {
    if (m.Type !== "bind" || !m.Target || !m.Source || m.Target === m.Source) continue;
    out = out.split(m.Target).join(m.Source);
  }
  return out;
}
```

**A `Sandboxes` for tests** (`sandbox.test.ts` line 39) overrides `prepareTools` and `buildImages`. The route tests also set the private `mount` so `start()` works; do the same in a subclass:

```typescript
class Ready extends Sandboxes {
  protected override prepareTools(): Promise<string | undefined> {
    (this as unknown as { mount: ToolsMount }).mount = { Type: "bind", Source: "/tmp/gm-tools", Target: "/opt/gm-tools", ReadOnly: true };
    return Promise.resolve(undefined);
  }
  protected override async buildImages(): Promise<{ image: string; clisVolume: string }> {
    await this.docker.createVolume("gm-clis-test");
    return { image: "img:1", clisVolume: "gm-clis-test" };
  }
}
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-paths.ts`

Pure: no file access, no `process.platform` (the platform is a required parameter). Imports: `path` from `node:path`, `RUN_VALUE_OPTIONS` from `graph-execution/api`, `type Workspace` from `./workspaces.js`. Use `path.win32` and `path.posix` explicitly, never plain `path.*`, so the results are the same on every OS.

- `containerRoot(ws, platform): string` — `ws.path` unless `platform === "win32"`; on `win32`, `/workspaces/` + `ws.rel` (`rel` already uses `/`).
- `toContainer(ws, hostPath, platform): string` — identity unless `win32`. On `win32`: normalise both `ws.path` and `hostPath` with `path.win32.normalize(p).replaceAll("\\", "/")` and drop trailing slashes; compare **case-insensitively**. Equal: `containerRoot`. `hostPath` starts with the workspace plus `/`: `containerRoot` plus the rest, with the rest's own case. Anything else (another drive, a sibling such as `hello-2`, a relative path): `hostPath` exactly as given.
- `toHost(ws, containerPath, platform): string` — identity unless `win32`. On `win32`: compare **case-sensitively** against `containerRoot` (after `path.posix.normalize`, trailing slashes dropped). Equal: `ws.path`. Inside: `ws.path` plus the rest, joined with the separator `ws.path` itself uses (`\` when `ws.path` contains one, else `/`). Anything else: unchanged.
- `toContainerArgs(ws, args, platform): string[]` — a copy unless `win32`. On `win32` the **path arguments** are: the first positional (the tasks folder) and the values of `--spec` and `--reviewers`, in both forms (`--spec x`, `--spec=x`). Walk the arguments as `scanArgs` does: the word after an option in `RUN_VALUE_OPTIONS` is its value, not a positional; after `--` everything is positional. A path argument that is `path.win32.isAbsolute` goes through `toContainer`; a relative one gets `\` replaced by `/` (PowerShell completes `.agents\tasks\x`, which is one file name on Linux). Every other argument is unchanged.
- **GOTCHA**: `toContainer`/`toHost` must also work when `ws.path` is a POSIX path and the platform is `win32`. That is how the integration test below runs on Linux and macOS: the mapping is applied to a real temp dir. This is why they normalise and compare strings and never call `path.win32.resolve` (it would add the current drive).

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-paths.test.ts`

Table tests (`it.each`) with a Windows-looking workspace literal and a POSIX one:

```typescript
const win: Workspace = { id: "github~octo~hello", path: "C:\\Users\\Me\\gm-ws\\github\\octo\\hello", rel: "github/octo/hello", forge: "github", fullPath: "octo/hello" };
const posix: Workspace = { ...win, path: "/tmp/gm/ws/github/octo/hello" };
const ROOT = "/workspaces/github/octo/hello";
```

| call | result |
| --- | --- |
| `containerRoot(win, "win32")` | `ROOT` |
| `containerRoot(win, "linux")`, `containerRoot(posix, "darwin")` | the workspace's own `path` |
| `containerRoot` of a workspace with `rel: "gitlab/group/sub/repo"` on `win32` | `/workspaces/gitlab/group/sub/repo` |
| `toContainer(win, win.path, "win32")`, also with a trailing `\` | `ROOT` |
| `toContainer(win, "c:\\users\\me\\GM-WS\\github\\octo\\hello\\Docs\\a.md", "win32")` | `ROOT + "/Docs/a.md"` |
| `toContainer(win, "C:/Users/Me/gm-ws/github/octo/hello/.graph-execution/gm-1", "win32")` | `ROOT + "/.graph-execution/gm-1"` |
| `toContainer(win, win.path + "/.graph-execution\\gm-1\\.ready.json", "win32")` | `ROOT + "/.graph-execution/gm-1/.ready.json"` |
| `toContainer(win, win.path + "\\docs\\..\\spec.md", "win32")` | `ROOT + "/spec.md"` |
| `toContainer` of `C:\Users\Me\gm-ws\github\octo\hello-2\x`, `…\octo\other\x`, `D:\x`, `docs\a.md` | unchanged |
| `toContainer(posix, posix.path + "/.graph-execution/r", "win32")` | `ROOT + "/.graph-execution/r"` |
| `toContainer(win, win.path + "\\a", "linux")`, `toContainer(posix, posix.path + "/a", "darwin")` | unchanged |
| `toHost(win, ROOT, "win32")`, also with a trailing `/` | `win.path` |
| `toHost(win, ROOT + "/docs/prd/a.md", "win32")` | `win.path + "\\docs\\prd\\a.md"` |
| `toHost(posix, ROOT + "/tasks", "win32")` | `/tmp/gm/ws/github/octo/hello/tasks` |
| `toHost` of `/workspaces/github/octo/hello-2/x`, `/workspaces/GitHub/octo/hello/x`, `/opt/gm-tools/x`, `C:\x`, `spec.md` on `win32` | unchanged |
| `toHost(win, ROOT + "/a", "linux")` | unchanged |

`toContainerArgs` on `win32` with `win` (and the same inputs unchanged on `"linux"`):

- `[win.path + "\\tasks\\x", "--spec", win.path + "\\docs\\x.md", "--provider", "fake"]` → `[ROOT + "/tasks/x", "--spec", ROOT + "/docs/x.md", "--provider", "fake"]`
- `[".agents\\tasks\\x", "--spec=docs\\prd\\x.md", "--reviewers", ".\\r.json", "--model", "a\\b"]` → `[".agents/tasks/x", "--spec=docs/prd/x.md", "--reviewers", "./r.json", "--model", "a\\b"]`
- `["--concurrency", "2", "tasks", "--spec", "spec.md", "extra\\word"]` → unchanged (`2` is a value; only the first positional is a path)
- `["--resume", "--run", "gm-1"]` and `["D:\\other\\tasks", "--spec", "D:\\other\\s.md"]` → unchanged

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `workspaceMount(ws, workspacesDir, self, override?, platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform)`: every `Target: ws.path` becomes `Target: containerRoot(ws, platform)`. With no `self` and no override on `win32` the result is `{ Type: "bind", Source: ws.path, Target: "/workspaces/<rel>" }`. Update the doc comment (line 215).
- **IMPLEMENT**: `sandboxEnv`'s `p` gets `gitConfig?: readonly (readonly [string, string])[]`. When it has entries, append at the very end `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=<n>` and, for each index `i`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<i>=<key>` and `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<i>=<value>`. Document `p.runDir` as "the run folder as the container sees it"; line 183 stays.
- **IMPLEMENT**: move `gitIdentity`'s inner `get` to a module function and add

```typescript
/** The git settings of a sandbox on a Windows host, for GIT_CONFIG_*: the mounted files look foreign-owned and executable. */
export async function windowsGitConfig(cwd: string): Promise<[string, string][]>
```

  It returns `["safe.directory", "*"]`, `["core.filemode", "false"]` and, when `git config --get core.autocrlf` in `cwd` prints a value, `["core.autocrlf", <value>]`; when it is unset, that entry is left out.
- **GOTCHA**: `containerBody` needs no change: it gets `owner`, `cwd` and `args` already in container form.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` (`start`, lines 558–611)

With `const pf = this.platform;`:

- **Owner**: `pf === "win32" ? { uid: 1000, gid: 1000 } : { uid: st2.uid, gid: st2.gid }` (`stat` reports uid 0 on Windows, and provider CLIs refuse to run unattended as root). The `chown` calls stay as they are (best effort, `.catch`).
- **Host paths stay host paths**: `runDir`, `readyFile`, `rm(readyFile)`, `mkdir(runDir)`, `writeFile(reviewersCopy)`, the reviewers read on resume and `existsSync(readyFile)` are graph-manager's own file access. Do not translate them.
- **Container form**: `sandboxEnv(process.env, { …, runDir: toContainer(p.ws, runDir, pf), …, ...(pf === "win32" ? { gitConfig: await windowsGitConfig(p.ws.path) } : {}) })`; ``env.push(`${REVIEWERS_ENV}=${toContainer(p.ws, reviewersCopy, pf)}`)``; `workspaceMount(p.ws, config.workspacesDir, this.self, config.sandboxWorkspacesSource, pf)`; in `containerBody`, `args: toContainerArgs(p.ws, p.args, pf)` and `cwd: toContainer(p.ws, p.cwd, pf)`.
- **GOTCHA**: `resuming` (line 574) reads `p.args`, not the translated copy; either works, keep it on `p.args`.
- **GOTCHA**: the tools mount needs no change: outside Docker its `Source` is `path.join(dataDir, "sandbox-tools")`, a Windows path on Windows, which Docker Desktop accepts as a bind source. `fillTools` already writes the wrapper with `\n` on every OS.
- **IMPLEMENT**: fix the comment at `routes/internal.ts` line 147: the args stay relative to `cwd`; `Sandboxes.start` maps `cwd` and the path arguments to the container's form on Windows.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runs.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `SandboxLookup` gets `/** The host platform of the sandbox service; default process.platform. */ readonly platform?: NodeJS.Platform;` (`Sandboxes` already has the field).
- **IMPLEMENT**: a helper `hostState(ws, state)`: when `state.sandbox` is undefined return `state`; else `{ ...state, tasksDir: toHost(ws, state.tasksDir, pf), specPath: toHost(ws, state.specPath, pf) }` with `pf = sandboxLookup?.platform ?? process.platform`. Apply it in `runDetail` to the state read at line 496, before it is used for `summarize`, `readTasks`, `graphOf` and the returned `detail.state`.
- **GOTCHA**: `pr.ts` (title from the spec, the move of the spec to `done/`) reads `specPath` only through `runDetail`, so it gets the host path without a change. `buildGraph(state)` and `summarize`'s own `readState` do not use the paths; leave them.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `startPassive` (line 335), `const file = bindRewrite(c, kv.slice("GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE=".length));`. With identical source and target (Linux, macOS) `bindRewrite` changes nothing.

### UPDATE the tests

- `sandbox-run.test.ts`: `workspaceMount` with `"win32"` as the fifth argument and a Windows-looking workspace gives `{ Type: "bind", Source: <its path>, Target: "/workspaces/github/octo/hello" }`, and with a volume override the target is the same; the existing expectations (default platform, POSIX workspace) stay. `sandboxEnv` with `gitConfig: [["safe.directory", "*"], ["core.filemode", "false"], ["core.autocrlf", "true"]]` ends with exactly `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=*`, … `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=true`; without `gitConfig`, no entry starts with `GIT_CONFIG_`. `windowsGitConfig` in a temp git repo: two entries when `core.autocrlf` is unset, a third `["core.autocrlf", "input"]` after `git config core.autocrlf input`.
  - **GOTCHA**: `vitest.config.ts` sets `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1` / `core.autocrlf=false` in the environment on Windows, and a machine's global or system config may set `core.autocrlf` too. In this test, save `process.env`, then delete `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, set `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and point `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at an empty temp file; restore everything in `finally` (as `docker.test.ts` does with `HOSTNAME`).
- `sandbox.test.ts`, one test, **no platform guard**: "on win32, mounts the workspace at /workspaces/<rel> and translates the paths". Make a real workspace at `<workspacesDir>/github/octo/hello` (`git init`, as `routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts` lines 24–33), write `<dataDir>/reviewers.json` (`{"reviewers":[]}`), build `new Ready({ config: testConfig(dir, { dockerSocket: f.socketPath, sandboxImage: "img:1" }), store, platform: "win32" })`, and call `start({ ws: resolveWorkspace(config.workspacesDir, "github~octo~hello")!, cwd: ws.path, args: [path.join(ws.path, "diamond"), "--spec", path.join(ws.path, "spec.md"), "--provider", "fake"], runId: "r1", providers: ["fake"] })`. Assert on the fake's container: `Config.User` is `1000:1000`; `Config.WorkingDir` is `/workspaces/github/octo/hello`; `HostConfig.Mounts[0]` equals `{ Type: "bind", Source: ws.path, Target: "/workspaces/github/octo/hello" }`; `Config.Cmd` is `["node", "/opt/gm-tools/graph-execution/dist/cli.js", "/workspaces/github/octo/hello/diamond", "--spec", "/workspaces/github/octo/hello/spec.md", "--provider", "fake", "--web-serve"]`; `Config.Env` contains `GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE=/workspaces/github/octo/hello/.graph-execution/r1/.ready.json`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS=/workspaces/github/octo/hello/.graph-execution/r1/.sandbox-reviewers.json`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=*`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.filemode`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=false`, and one entry matching `/^GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=[23]$/`. `start` resolving proves the ready file was found at the **host** path; also assert that `.ready.json` and `.sandbox-reviewers.json` exist under `path.join(ws.path, ".graph-execution", "r1")`. On Linux and macOS the host path is POSIX, so this test exercises the mapping of a real folder; the Windows path shapes are covered by the pure tables.
- `runs.test.ts`, in `runDetail`: put the task files in `<wsDir>/tasks`, write the state with `sandbox: { image: "img:1" }`, `tasksDir: "/workspaces/github/octo/hello/tasks"`, `specPath: "/workspaces/github/octo/hello/spec.md"`, call `setSandboxLookup({ pageOf: async () => undefined, platform: "win32" })` (reset it with `setSandboxLookup(undefined)` in `finally`), and expect `detail.state.tasksDir` to be `path.join(wsDir, "tasks")`, `detail.state.specPath` to be `path.join(wsDir, "spec.md")`, and the graph to have the edge `["1", "2"]` (the folder was read). A second case without `sandbox` in the state leaves the same paths unchanged.
- `routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts` (lines 83–99) and `routes/internal.test.ts` (lines 120, 129) run with the real platform, which is `win32` on Windows CI: compute the expectations with the pure functions and `process.platform`. With `const ws = resolveWorkspace(c.config.workspacesDir, WS)!`: `Config.User` is `"1000:1000"` on `win32`, else the `stat` owner; `WorkingDir` is `toContainer(ws, <host cwd>, process.platform)`; the workspace mount is `{ Type: "bind", Source: wsDir, Target: containerRoot(ws, process.platform) }`; the reviewers variable is `toContainer(ws, copy, process.platform)`. The file checks on `copy` keep the host path.
- `sandbox-tools.test.ts` (the test at line 41): add `expect(readFileSync(wrapper, "utf8")).not.toContain("\r")`.

## Engine facts and limits (no engine change; do not "fix" these)

- The engine resolves everything from its working directory inside the container, so `state.json` holds container paths on Windows: `tasksDir`, `specPath` and each task's `worktree` (`/workspaces/<rel>/.graph-execution/<run>/worktrees/…`). Worktrees are created inside the workspace's run folder. A resume in a new container sees the same paths, because the container path depends only on `rel`.
- git's worktree records under `<workspace>/.git/worktrees/` hold container paths too. On the Windows host, `git worktree list` shows them as prunable. graph-manager never runs `git worktree` commands, and `scan()` only lists them; leave that alone.
- The run lock's host line is the container's hostname (`sbx-<hex>`), foreign to the host as on Linux; Resume already handles it (`routes/resume.ts` lines 44–60).
- graph-manager reads only `tasksDir` and `specPath` as paths from a sandboxed run's state; task rows use commit ids.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `sandbox-paths.ts` exports `containerRoot`, `toContainer`, `toHost`, `toContainerArgs` with a required `platform`; every row of the tables passes on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- [ ] `new Sandboxes({ …, platform: "win32" }).start(…)` against the fake daemon creates a container with `User: "1000:1000"`, `WorkingDir: "/workspaces/<rel>"`, the workspace bind `{ Source: <host path>, Target: "/workspaces/<rel>" }`, the ready file and reviewers variables in container form, the `GIT_CONFIG_*` entries (`safe.directory=*`, `core.filemode=false`, and `core.autocrlf` only when the workspace has a value), translated path arguments, and returns once the ready file exists at the host path.
- [ ] With the default platform on Linux and macOS, the create body of a sandboxed start is unchanged, and `git diff` shows no change to `containerBody`.
- [ ] `runDetail` of a run whose state has `sandbox` returns `tasksDir` and `specPath` in host form on `win32` (and its graph from the task files); other runs and other platforms are untouched.
- [ ] `scripts/fake-docker.mjs` writes the ready file through the bind mounts.
- [ ] No engine file, README, wiki page or `TESTING.md` changed.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass at the repository root; no test is skipped on a platform except those already guarded.

## Validation commands

```bash
# From apps/graph-manager: the tests of this slice
npx vitest run src/server/sandbox-paths.test.ts src/server/sandbox-run.test.ts src/server/sandbox.test.ts src/server/runs.test.ts
npx vitest run src/server/routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts src/server/routes/internal.test.ts src/server/routes/resume.test.ts src/server/routes/pr.test.ts src/server/sandbox.e2e.test.ts

# From the repository root: everything
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
```

`sandbox.e2e.test.ts` runs only on Linux with the engine built (`npm run build -w graph-execution`); it must still pass with the default platform. Known environment failure, not caused by this slice: `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` "exits 2 at startup when --provider claude is not on the PATH" fails wherever a real `claude` is installed next to `node`. CI is the judge for it.
